newsitem.title: USA: Gap shares fall on flat August same-store sales.
newsitem.headline: Gap shares fall on flat August same-store sales.

text.p: The stock of Gap Inc. fell sharply Thursday after the San Francisco-based retailer reported disappointing August sales.

The apparel company said sales at stores open for more than a year were unchanged last month, after rising 7 percent in July and 12 percent in June. Overall sales for August rose 19 percent to $441 million.
Gap Chief Financial Officer Warren Hashagen attributed the flat same-store sales to several factors, including weakness in basic denim products ahead of the start of the new school year.
"We had a weak performance from Gap, particularly in the basic five-pocket jeans category," he said in a telephone interview.
Hashagen noted better performance at other divisions. "August came in flat, but it includes strong performances from both Gap Kids and Old Navy," he said.
"The basic entry price-point denim business is a back-to-school business, so it should not be the same issue in the September," he said.

Hashagen said sales at Banana Republic were also lackluster. He said Gap's success in the rest of the third quarter and the balance of the year will depend on fashion assortments, which sold well in August.
Gap shares fell $4.875 to 29 in active trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
Some analysts suggsted the weak sales figures could affect Gap's earnings for the third quarter.
"Their overall sales are up, but same store sales are flat and that could be a precursor of poor earnings," said Hildergard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities.
Other analysts said Gap's flat sales could reflect a reluctance on the part of the company to mark down merchandise.
"GAP chose not to be promotional," said Elizabeth Pierce of Stephens Inc.
Unlike other retailers it competes with for back-to-school business, she said Gap did not offer price markdowns on denim goods. While this hurt sales, it did not damage its bottom line.
"They can do what they need to do to manage the business for future profitability," Pierce said.
As of Aug. 31, Gap operated 1,779 stores compared to 1,602 at Aug. 26, 1995, up 11 percent.
